comments.body:
🟡 **Version option casing blocks generation** With `version: Version` configured for a lowercase `version` column, `postgresReferencesColumn` rejects writes that reference the column. [MapColumn](https://github.com/gosuda/spira/blob/6031a63255bc7496e22b38921e10401a2d50c291/orm/table.lgo#L115-L124 "orm/table.lgo:115-124") accepts either spelling, but the generation check compares the SQL name to the raw option.
Learn more The version option identifies the column an entity uses for optimistic locking. [buildVersions](https://github.com/gosuda/spira/blob/6031a63255bc7496e22b38921e10401a2d50c291/cmd/sqlc-gen-spira/model.lgo#L1237-L1255 "cmd/sqlc-gen-spira/model.lgo:1237-1255") stores that option without resolving it to the catalog column. [MapColumn](https://github.com/gosuda/spira/blob/6031a63255bc7496e22b38921e10401a2d50c291/orm/table.lgo#L115-L124 "orm/table.lgo:115-124") resolves the same option case-insensitively, but [postgresReferencesColumn](https://github.com/gosuda/spira/blob/6031a63255bc7496e22b38921e10401a2d50c291/cmd/sqlc-gen-spira/version_reference.lgo#L22-L36 "cmd/sqlc-gen-spira/version_reference.lgo:22-36") requires exact equality with the SQL identifier. Consequently, the generator reports a missing version column even when the SQL references the column that the ORM would map. **Example:** Set `tables.items.version` to `Version` and generate [UpdateItem](https://github.com/gosuda/spira/blob/6031a63255bc7496e22b38921e10401a2d50c291/cmd/sqlc-gen-spira/testdata/postgresql/db/queries/items.sql#L6-L9 "cmd/sqlc-gen-spira/testdata/postgresql/db/queries/items.sql:6-9") against the lowercase `version` column. Both the assignment and the predicate name that column, but generation returns `writes versioned table items without Version`. **Recommended fix:** Resolve the PostgreSQL version option against the table catalog before storing it in `buildVersions`. Prefer an exact match, then apply the supported case-insensitive lookup when the match is unambiguous. Compare SQL tokens against the resolved catalog name so distinct quoted identifiers remain distinct. Add a generation test for a mixed-case option and a control for a quoted mixed-case column.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Versioned writes rejected in materialized CTEs** When a write uses `AS MATERIALIZED`, `excludeReferenceDeclarations` hides the version column inside the CTE body. Generation fails if that body contains the only real version references.
Learn more A PostgreSQL common table expression can contain an `UPDATE` and expose its returned rows to the outer statement. [writeTargets](https://github.com/gosuda/spira/blob/6031a63255bc7496e22b38921e10401a2d50c291/cmd/sqlc-gen-spira/model.lgo#L1112-L1132 "cmd/sqlc-gen-spira/model.lgo:1112-1132") detects the update inside the CTE. The declaration pass treats `MATERIALIZED` after `AS` as a declared name and excludes the parenthesized statement after it. [postgresReferencesColumn](https://github.com/gosuda/spira/blob/6031a63255bc7496e22b38921e10401a2d50c291/cmd/sqlc-gen-spira/version_reference.lgo#L22-L36 "cmd/sqlc-gen-spira/version_reference.lgo:22-36") then ignores genuine version references inside the write itself; this is independent of binding names across scopes. **Example:** `WITH bumped AS MATERIALIZED (UPDATE items SET version = version + 1 RETURNING id) SELECT id FROM bumped;` updates `version`, but generation reports that the query writes `items` without `version`. **Recommended fix:** Recognize `AS MATERIALIZED (...)` in CTE declarations and leave the body visible to the reference scan. Keep excluding actual declaration lists and cast modifiers. Add matching generator cases for a materialized CTE that updates `version` and one that omits it.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔍 **No pipeline coverage for alias refusals** The role tests call `Generate` with fixture SQL directly. [readSQLcLiteralInputs](https://github.com/gosuda/spira/blob/6031a63255bc7496e22b38921e10401a2d50c291/cmd/sqlc-gen-spira/sqlc_postgres_literal_test.lgo#L85-L89 "cmd/sqlc-gen-spira/sqlc_postgres_literal_test.lgo:85-89") omits those fixtures, so no alias refusal is asserted on SQL emitted by sqlc. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

review_snapshot.scope: The two r40 findings remain resolved. These three later findings are not claimed fixed by the completed r40 verification.

proof_retirement.scope: Only the owned terminal proof workflow is removed; source/proof history and failed receipts are preserved.

observer_path.reason: Actual test launcher prepended GOROOT/bin; initial PATH-only observer omitted nested records.

limitations: The reference guard checks syntactic column presence; it does not perform full table binding across nested query or CTE scopes.

The exact unaliased OPERATOR query remains native/direct-generator positive; the existing SQLc output-column alias refusal still occurs before version checking. The unqualified operator(name) spelling remains an upstream syntax-error control, with its exact SQL bytes preserved.
Sloplint passed the unchanged major threshold: zero blocker/critical/major, one minor generic-name finding in unchanged web/web.lgo Handle, and 12 skips.
Eject completed and actual stock Go 1.27.4 built the output. Existing dependency-capability and frontend node_modules symlink warnings remain; stock-Go tests and just engines were not claimed.
The maintained Spira source contains no ordinary GitHub Actions or Depot workflow. The isolated Depot proof supplies source-gate evidence; it is not an ordinary PR CI run.
Earlier failed runs remain failures. No failed full-source gate was reused.
next_action: Own the three new reference-option, materialized-CTE and permanent-pipeline findings on a separate isolated r41 proof. Keep r40 retired and preserve its completed and failed evidence.
